title: State of Karnataka v. Mohan Kumar @ Cyanide Mohan
court_or_authority: High Court of Karnataka / Fast Track Sessions Court, Mangalore
legal_citation: Criminal Appeal No. 411/2014 (Karnataka HC); Sessions Case No. 89/2010
source: High Court of Karnataka Official Judgment & Indian Kanoon (doc/135245842)
evidence: Forensic laboratory detection of potassium cyanide in hotel drain traps and viscera samples
Recovery of stolen gold ornaments from local pawn and jewelry brokers in Mangalore
Fake government identity cards and forged marriage affidavit stationery recovered from residence
Multiple cyanide pills disguised as contraceptive tablets recovered upon apprehension
Call data records (CDR) linking suspect SIM card to 20 victim mobile handsets prior to disappearances
modus_operandi: Befriends women from financially modest backgrounds under the false pretext of marriage proposal. Escorts them to lodge rooms in towns distant from their residence. Convinces victims to consume cyanide disguised as contraceptive medicine near bus stations or hotel washrooms. Takes deceased's jewelry, gold, and cash before departing scene.
personality_disorder: Clinical behavioral analysis documented in trial court records: Antisocial Personality Disorder (Psychopathy) with extreme pathological deceit, absence of remorse, instrumental aggression, and cold financial exploitation.
common_traits: Use of fast-acting lethal chemical poison (Potassium Cyanide)
Theft of gold jewelry and liquid cash post-mortem
Execution of murder in transit public transit hubs or hotels
Repeated clinical execution without emotional affect
summary: Landmark Karnataka serial homicide case involving 20 victims between 2003 and 2009. The High Court of Karnataka and Sessions Court Mangalore convicted the accused across multiple consecutive trials based on recovered cyanide stores, CDR corroboration, and pawned jewelry recovery, confirming capital sentences commuted to life without remission.
